speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your post-operative review. I understand you are experiencing occasional shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings after your tympanoplasty. To help me pinpoint the issue, can you describe exactly where the pain is located and what triggers it?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Otitis Media with recurrent cholesteatoma.

The patient's history of chronic bilateral ear infections, combined with new-onset shooting pain triggered by chewing (suggesting Eustachian tube dysfunction or referred pain from mastoid involvement) and persistent discomfort with earrings post-tympanoplasty, strongly suggests a recurrence of disease within the mastoid or a cholesteatoma that may have been missed or recurred after surgery. Given the 20 dB hearing improvement but persistent symptoms, we need to confirm the status of the middle ear. REQUEST IMAGES: High-Resolution CT Temporal Bone (right side) and Microscopic Otoscopy.
